design: CanonicalIngestionEnvelope is LLD v1.1 section 2.5's closed envelope restricted to the fields this task's own acceptance criteria require (partition order via aggregate_ref/sequence, correlation_id/causation_id, classification_marking_ref, source_ref provenance, idempotency_key); publish() keys every Kafka record by aggregate_ref so Kafka's own partitioner preserves per-aggregate order, checks the registered-schema allow-list and the aggregate's own last-published sequence BEFORE ever calling the real producer CLI, and quarantines (never publishes) an unknown schema or an out-of-order sequence; publish_from_mapping() additionally catches a missing/malformed governed-context field at construction time and quarantines it too -- all three of this task's negative-acceptance conditions, made structural and enforced before any real Kafka write

residual_risks: This backbone self-provisions a fresh, disposable broker per instance rather than depending on the shared ocor-bootstrap Kafka; a caller wanting a long-lived production topic across many CanonicalEventBackbone instances would need to reuse the same container name across calls, which this task's own smallest-slice scope does not need to expose.

publish()'s idempotency check (an in-memory _seen_idempotency_keys set) is scoped to one CanonicalEventBackbone instance's own lifetime; a real production deployment with multiple producer processes would need a durable idempotency store (e.g. keyed in C3's own canonical commit, which already owns idempotency for the canonical effect itself) -- this backbone's own idempotency check is a defense-in-depth safety net for a single producer's own retries, not the sole idempotency boundary of the system.

The 'partition order' guarantee relies on Kafka's own key-based partitioner routing identical keys (aggregate_ref) to the identical partition, which is the standard, well-established Kafka contract this task deliberately relies on rather than re-implementing a custom partitioner.

The pre-existing local-venv gap noted in prior evidence (uv cannot resolve the exact 3.12.11 interpreter in this sandbox) is unchanged and out of this task's scope; it produces the same 2 pre-existing, unrelated regression failures documented in every prior evidence file this session.
rollback_procedure_verified: Every test provisions a fresh, uniquely-named, isolated broker and destroys it (container + volume) in a fixture teardown, verified directly by 4 consecutive full test-suite runs plus the full regression run with no leaked containers or volumes between runs (docker ps confirmed at most one ocor-c5-backbone-* container alive at any time during concurrent local test execution).
